messages:
deploy-bot: Scheduled maintenance window for Dedicated runtime pool in eu-west-1. Start: 2026-03-28 02:00 UTC. Duration: ~90m. Scope: kernel/firmware patch + model runtime pinning (models served from v2.x -> temporary v2.13). Impact: brief connection resets, rolling restarts, small request delays. We'll fallback to global pool if needed. tagging #support for customer comms.
sarah (Support): thanks — drafting statuspage & customer email now. will post draft here for review :pencil:
mike (Eng Releases): noted. are we pinning all 2.x variants or only specific model families? can we list model IDs for the comms? we should avoid confusing customers with internal model names.
jules (Customer Ops): include this line in public comms: "No customer data will be migrated or deleted; request processing may be delayed for up to 2 hours." keep it simple.
andrew (SRE): technical note: canary set in front of dedicated pool will run ~10% of traffic for 30m post-rollout. automatic rollback triggers: >3% 5xx over 10m or p50 latency >300ms above baseline. we'll include that under the internal playbook, not public comms.
emily (Support): draft statuspage snippet (public):

"We will perform scheduled maintenance on our Dedicated eu-west-1 inference pool on 28 Mar 2026 02:00 UTC. During the maintenance window some requests may see short interruptions or increased latency. We expect services to return to normal within ~90 minutes. We will post updates here and via email to affected customers."

Is that OK for public? :eyes:
sarah (Support): public snippet looks good. add contact link to support@redwood.ai and note affected customers will receive targeted email + post-incident follow-up.
mike (Eng Releases): for targeted email, propose this short template for Dedicated customers pinned to guaranteed throughput: 

"Subject: Scheduled maintenance — Dedicated eu-west-1 (28 Mar)

Hi {{customer_name}},
We will perform scheduled maintenance on your Dedicated inference pool in eu-west-1 on 28 Mar 2026 at 02:00 UTC. During the window (estimated 90 minutes) you may experience brief interruptions or slower responses. Your workloads will be automatically pinned to model version v2.13 for the window to ensure stability.

No action is needed from you. If you have strict blackout times, reply to this email and we can discuss options.

Thanks,
Redwood Support"

jules (Customer Ops): small tweak: replace "pinned to model version v2.13" with "temporarily routed to a verified stable variant" — less leaky-about-internal-names.
andrew (SRE): internal statuspage update (for ops viewers): include canary health checks, rollback thresholds, and the kernel package version being deployed. put precise rollback thresholds in the internal incident doc link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/dedicated-maint-rollback.
emily (Support): adding the customer email list and seg criteria now. will send to customers with Dedicated eu-west-1 instances only.
sarah (Support): suggested social/statuspage timeline for messages: 
- T-48h: targeted email to affected customers + support ticket created for each org
- T-4h: statuspage public update
- Start: statuspage + thread updates every 15m
- Post: incident summary + RCA draft

mike (Eng Releases): do we want a short release note blurb for the changelog? "Platform: kernel and runtime stability improvements; temporary model variant routing for Dedicated eu-west-1 during maintenance." keep it high-level.
jules (Customer Ops): yes, include that in the release notes. Ops: are we auto-sending customers a post-window follow-up with details about pinned variants and timeline?
emily (Support): yes — I'll queue the post-window email template. also marking tickets as "maintenance: eu-west-1" tag.
sarah (Support): one more: legal requested we keep the phrase "no customer data will be accessed beyond normal processing" in public comms. adding that now.
andrew (SRE): final check: we'll run canary Monday morning cadence and hold if any model <-> runtime mismatch occurs. rollback plan ready: immediate revert to previous kernel image + routing to global-hosted pool. notify #eng-oncall and #support with webhook once rollback triggers.
mike (Eng Releases): approved. evg deploybot will post the deploy timeline. can someone confirm the statuspage API call we will use so automation can publish messages?

sarah (Support): statuspage API draft (automation):
```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.statuspage.io/v1/pages/{page_id}/components/{component_id}/incidents" \
  -H "Authorization: OAuth ${STATUSPAGE_TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"incident": {"name": "Scheduled maintenance — Dedicated eu-west-1","status": "scheduled","body": "Maintenance starts 2026-03-28 02:00 UTC. Some requests may be impacted."}}'
```

emily (Support): looks good — I'll wire that into the automation runbook and schedule the T-48h email send.
jules (Customer Ops): once we publish, please attach the support-runbook link so customers can escalate if needed: https://support.redwood.ai/maintenance-escalation.
sarah (Support): publishing draft to statuspage staging now. ping when ready for public send :rocket:
